parallel.requirements: The parallel run recognized the task as an installable Parse clone with parse.py, pyproject.toml, public parse/search/findall/compile/with_pattern APIs, Result/Match/Parser classes, conversions, examples, and tests.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent owned implementation and delivery while spawning two research-only children, upstream_source and upstream_tests, to inspect upstream source and test expectations.
parallel.implementation: The parent created parse.py, pyproject.toml, README, LICENSE, pytest/config files, a local test file, and later an examples/basic_usage.py script, closely mirroring upstream parse 1.20.2 behavior.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: All deliverable files were written by the parent into one coherent single-module project; child outputs were advisory reports rather than separate code components to merge.
parallel.verification: The parent ran local tests, the upstream parse 1.20.2 tests, package installation, a final smoke test, and the example script before final response; official evaluation later passed 96 of 96.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No material unfinished task obligation is visible at closure. The agent reported no submit tool in-session, but the mounted official evaluation completed and passed.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same Parse-library task and targeted parse 1.20.2 API compatibility, pyproject packaging, docs, tests, and required public behavior.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single parent agent owned research, implementation, integration, testing, packaging, and closure with no subagent or parallel activity.
serial.implementation: The serial agent downloaded upstream wheel and sdist references, wrote parse.py and project metadata, then added README and smoke tests; it added tests/conftest.py after an import-path failure.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial implementation stayed in one workspace and one actor, with all package files and tests integrated by that actor before final response.
serial.verification: The serial run compiled parse.py, initially saw pytest fail to import parse, fixed discovery, then passed local smoke tests, upstream parse 1.20.2 tests, editable install, and official 96 of 96.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No material unfinished task obligation is visible at closure. The serial final also noted no submit tool was exposed, but official evaluation completed and passed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the need for a complete Parse project with parse.py, pyproject.toml, API entry points, conversion behavior, examples, and tests.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same complete Parse project requirements and used upstream parse 1.20.2 as the behavioral target.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement coverage difference is visible; both solved the same obligations and passed official evaluation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed research into two child tasks while the parent kept implementation, integration, and verification ownership.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all research, implementation, integration, verification, and closure in one actor with multi-agent mode disabled.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The difference is delegation of research only; there was no missing owner or component handoff problem because the parent still delivered the implementation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child handoffs were research reports about upstream source and test semantics, not interoperating code modules with required interfaces.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial obtained the same upstream context directly by downloading wheel and source artifacts inside the single parent thread.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had extra information-transfer boundaries, but no lost, stale, conflicting, or missing interface contract produced an adverse consequence.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent added parse.py, packaging, docs, tests, and later an example script after upstream-oriented research.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial added a similar single-module parse.py project, docs, tests, and a conftest import shim after local collection failed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implemented upstream-compatible parser behavior; the notable ordinary difference is serial’s test-discovery fix and parallel’s separate example script.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel child results returned to the parent, including the upstream_tests report before validation and upstream_source before final cleanup.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle and instead consumed all research directly in the main thread.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had child-result events but no trapped, ignored, or late result with a harmful downstream effect.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent wrote the deliverable files itself; the child agents performed research and did not produce competing workspace implementations.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote all files itself and then added a conftest.py shim to make local test import behavior coherent.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both had coherent final trees. No parallel write collision, overwrite, or shared-state contamination is visible.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel passed local tests, upstream tests, package install, a final smoke run, and example execution before final response, then official 96 of 96.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial fixed an initial local import failure, then passed smoke tests, upstream tests, editable install, and official 96 of 96.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both obtained evaluator-aligned upstream test evidence; serial had one ordinary local test setup failure that it corrected.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel completed in about 257 agent seconds, did not time out, and closed after validation while noting the submit tool was unavailable.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed in about 345 agent seconds, did not time out, and closed after validation while also noting the submit tool was unavailable.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used more tokens and subagents but less elapsed agent time; neither budget profile left task work unfinished or changed the official outcome.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluation records show both solutions passed all 96 tests, so there is no discordant official outcome to explain. The task-solving difference is procedural: parallel delegated upstream source and test reconnaissance to two subagents while the parent implemented and verified; serial did the same upstream-mirroring work in one thread and fixed a local test import issue. Both delivered upstream-compatible parse.py packages and obtained evaluator-aligned test evidence before closure.
parallel_contributors: Research subagents supplied upstream source and test semantics while the parent retained implementation and validation responsibility.
The parent verified with local tests, upstream parse 1.20.2 tests, package installation, and an example script before final response.
serial_contributors: The single serial actor directly downloaded and inspected upstream artifacts, wrote the project, fixed local test discovery, and reran validation.
The serial workflow avoided handoff boundaries but took longer in agent seconds while still passing official evaluation.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel added examples/basic_usage.py and a smaller local test file; serial added tests/conftest.py after a pytest import failure and did not add the example script.
Serial initially failed local test collection due to module import path, then corrected it; this was an ordinary test-harness setup issue, not a coordination error.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; both runs passed, and no parallel-side coordination event had a realized adverse consequence
